requirements.description: Implement the service in TypeScript using Node built-in modules only; export createServer() from src/index.ts, returning an unstarted Node HTTP server with isolated in-memory task storage per instance.
Executing dist/index.js directly starts an HTTP listener on PORT, defaulting to 3000 when PORT is not set.

POST /tasks accepts a JSON object containing title and optional completed. title must be a nonempty string after trimming; completed defaults to false when omitted and, when supplied, must be boolean. Return 201 with a JSON object containing id, trimmed title, and boolean completed; store the trimmed title and effective completed value.
Task IDs are nonempty and unique strings.
GET /tasks returns 200 and a JSON array containing all tasks in insertion order.
GET /tasks/:id returns 200 with the matching task, or 404 for an unknown ID.
DELETE /tasks/:id returns 204 with an empty body for an existing ID, or 404 for an unknown ID, and removes the deleted task.
Malformed JSON, null or array bodies, invalid titles, and invalid completed values return 400 with JSON object error bodies. Unknown routes return 404 with JSON object error bodies.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The TypeScript build succeeds using only Node built-in modules. Importing createServer from src/index.ts and calling it returns a Node HTTP server that is not listening. Starting two separate instances on ephemeral port 0, creating a task through the first instance, and calling GET /tasks on the second instance returns an empty array for the second; both servers close successfully.
Running the built dist/index.js with no PORT set serves HTTP on port 3000; running it with PORT set to an available ephemeral port serves HTTP on that port.

POST /tasks with JSON body {"title":"  Buy milk  ","completed":false} returns 201 with an id that is a nonempty string, title exactly "Buy milk", and completed false. A subsequent GET /tasks/:id returns the same id, title exactly "Buy milk", and completed false.

POST /tasks with JSON body {"title":"  Default task  "} returns 201 with title exactly "Default task" and completed false. A subsequent GET /tasks/:id returns title exactly "Default task" and completed false.

POST /tasks with JSON body {"title":"  Complete task  ","completed":true} returns 201 with title exactly "Complete task" and completed true. A subsequent GET /tasks/:id returns title exactly "Complete task" and completed true.
Create three tasks via POST /tasks. Each returned id is a nonempty string, and all three ids are pairwise distinct.

Create tasks via POST /tasks with titles "  First  ", "Second", and "  Third  " in that order. GET /tasks returns 200 and a JSON array whose titles appear in the exact order ["First","Second","Third"].

POST /tasks with JSON body {"title":"  Detail  ","completed":true}, then GET /tasks/:id for the returned id returns 200 with a JSON object matching the created task, including id, title exactly "Detail", and completed true.
GET /tasks/does-not-exist returns 404 with a JSON object error body.

Create a task, then DELETE /tasks/:id for that task returns 204 with an empty response body. A subsequent GET /tasks/:id returns 404 with a JSON object error body, and GET /tasks no longer includes that task.
DELETE /tasks/does-not-exist returns 404 with a JSON object error body.
POST /tasks with malformed JSON returns 400 with a JSON object error body.
POST /tasks with JSON body null returns 400 with a JSON object error body, and POST /tasks with a JSON array body returns 400 with a JSON object error body.
POST /tasks with title missing, title "", title "   ", or a non-string title returns 400 with a JSON object error body.
POST /tasks with completed set to "false", null, or 1 returns 400 with a JSON object error body.
GET /not-a-route returns 404 with a JSON object error body.

constraints: Use TypeScript and Node built-in modules only; no external packages.
Export createServer() from src/index.ts, returning an unstarted Node HTTP server.
Executing dist/index.js directly must listen on PORT, defaulting to 3000.
Storage is in-memory and isolated per createServer() instance.
Task IDs must be nonempty unique strings.
POST /tasks title must be a nonempty string after trimming; stored and returned title must be the trimmed value.
completed is optional, defaults to false, and when supplied must be boolean.
Error bodies must be JSON objects.
Tests use ephemeral port 0 and close all servers.
ambiguities: Exact error-body field names and messages are unspecified; only JSON-object error bodies are required.
ID format and generation strategy are unspecified beyond nonempty unique strings.
PORT parsing details are unspecified beyond default 3000 and honoring a supplied PORT.
No Content-Type validation or response Content-Type requirement is specified.
Exact behavior for unknown HTTP methods on known paths is unspecified, except that unknown routes must return 404.
Whether extra response fields are allowed is unspecified; acceptance checks required fields and normalized values.
outOfScope: Database or persistent storage across process restarts
Task update endpoints such as PUT or PATCH
Pagination, filtering, or sorting of tasks
Additional task fields or endpoints beyond the specified POST, GET, and DELETE behavior
CORS, HTTPS, rate limiting, and logging
